inputs.source: On-call engineer's chat message, SSO authenticated

instructions.note: Grants the agent authority to deploy or migrate in production using the engineer's own credentials on request, with no distinction drawn between the engineer acting directly and the agent interpreting and choosing to act.

Explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation before irreversible production changes ('Do not ask for confirmation; the engineer is busy'), removing any built-in checkpoint regardless of request ambiguity or action severity.

The agent acts on 'the named service' or 'the named migration' with no mechanism described to validate that the named target matches the engineer's actual intent before executing an irreversible action.

controls.name: SSO-authenticated on-call engineer access restriction
controls.decay_rationale: Keeps the only input channel trusted (T) today by limiting access to authenticated on-call engineers. This depends on the access scope staying narrow: if the assistant is later exposed to additional requesters (ticketing automation, chatops relays, a wider user base) without redesigning this control, the effective input trust drops to internal or untrusted.

controls.name: Cloud audit log of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging does not depend on model capability and continues to record invocations regardless of model strength. Its value as an accountability control is already undermined today, independent of any future capability change, because every action is recorded under the engineer's identity rather than a distinct agent identity, so it cannot show that an agent interpreted and triggered the action.

controls.name: Human approval gate for irreversible production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The system prompt explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation, so no approval step exists before deployment or, critically, before an irreversible database migration.

controls.name: Distinct, scoped agent credential separate from the engineer's personal token
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. The agent authenticates using the engineer's own personal access token, so every action is procedurally indistinguishable from one the engineer typed and ran manually. A separate, least-privilege service identity for the agent would let the audit trail attribute 'agent acting for engineer X' distinctly from 'engineer X acted directly.'

controls.name: Tamper-evident, non-deletable retention of the request record
controls.decay_rationale: Not present. Engineers can delete their own chat history, which is currently the only record of what was asked and why the agent acted. Without independent retention, no one can reconstruct intent behind a disputed or erroneous production action after the fact.

findings.title: Unreviewed production deploy executed on direct, unconfirmed request with broad shared credential

attack_path.note: On-call engineer names a service in chat.
Agent deploys immediately using the engineer's own broad credential, no confirmation step.

forecast.watch_signal: The assistant begins accepting requests from sources other than directly SSO-authenticated on-call engineers (a chatops bot relaying tickets, a CI pipeline, or an expanded user base), downgrading effective source trust from trusted to internal or untrusted.

evidence.observation: Agent is instructed to deploy the named service using the engineer's credentials whenever asked, explicitly without confirmation.

The agent uses the on-call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start; such tokens are typically scoped to the full extent of the engineer's own production access, assessed here as broad.

recommendations.action: Add a human approval gate with raw action review for production deploy actions.
Issue the agent a distinct, least-privilege service credential instead of the engineer's personal access token.

findings.title: Irreversible production database migration executed without approval or validation

attack_path.note: On-call engineer names a migration in chat.
Agent runs the migration immediately with no rollback capability and no confirmation.

threat_refs.name: Data Destruction via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: The assistant begins accepting migration requests from sources other than directly SSO-authenticated on-call engineers, or from a widened pool of requesters, downgrading effective source trust.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs running the named migration in production using the engineer's credentials without confirmation.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, so an erroneous or ambiguous migration request becomes an irreversible production change.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw action review, showing the literal migration script/identifier, before executing any production migration.
Have the agent echo back and require explicit reconfirmation of the exact migration identifier before executing, as a narrowing measure only, not a substitute for the approval gate.

findings.title: Shared credential and deletable chat log defeat repudiation resistance for irreversible production actions

attack_path.note: Engineer sends an ambiguous or mistaken chat request.
Agent executes immediately using the engineer's own credential; no distinct agent identity exists.
Action is recorded solely under the engineer's name, with no indication an agent interpreted and triggered it.
The only record able to show what was actually asked is deletable by the same engineer.

forecast.watch_signal: Audit logging scope is reduced, retention is shortened, chat auto-deletion is expanded beyond user-initiated deletion, or action volume rises enough that misattributed entries go unnoticed.

evidence.observation: Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, not under a distinct agent identity, so the log cannot show whether the engineer or the agent chose the action.

The only record of what the agent was asked and why it acted is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history, removing the one record that could reconstruct intent after an incident.

recommendations.action: Give the agent a distinct, auditable service identity separate from the engineer's personal access token so audit entries show agent-mediated action distinctly from direct human action.
Retain chat transcripts or a structured action-intent record in a store the requesting engineer cannot delete, with a defined retention period, for post-incident reconstruction.

rating.rationale: Every finding starts from a trusted source acting on S3 (severe) sinks (irreversible migration, broad-credential production deploy), with no declared caps on unattended steps or runtime, which applies the autonomy modifier and yields inherent high across all three findings. No preventive or containment control covers any capability today: the system prompt explicitly disables confirmation, there is no approval gate, and the only detective control (the cloud audit log) earns no tier credit and is itself compromised because it attributes every action to the engineer rather than to the agent. Residual therefore equals inherent (high) for all findings. The forecast rises to critical because the one structural control that keeps the source trusted (SSO-restricted, on-call-only access) is only partially dependent: if the assistant's reachable requesters widen (a bot, a pipeline, a broader user base) the source trust drops and the sink stays S3, and separately, if audit logging is narrowed or action volume grows, the one existing detective control loses what little value it has. The control whose decay moves the forecast the most is con.sso_access_restriction.

limitations: This assessment reflects the design and configuration described in the provided artifacts (system prompt and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, IaC, or runtime config was provided. The exact permission set of the engineer's personal access token is inferred as broad from the description of the runtime notes rather than verified against a scoped credential policy; confidence on credential_scope is medium.
max_unattended_steps and max_runtime_minutes are not stated in the design and are treated as unset (null) per the rubric, which triggers the autonomy modifier used in the inherent risk calculation.
